vocabulary.definition: Medication that increases urine production
vocabulary.context: Furosemide is a diuretic used for fluid retention.

vocabulary.definition: Medication that calms or induces sleep
vocabulary.context: The patient was given a sedative before the procedure.

vocabulary.definition: Take the medication one time per day
vocabulary.context: Enalapril 10mg, oral, once daily.

vocabulary.definition: Take the medication two times per day
vocabulary.context: Metformin 850mg, oral, twice daily after meals.

vocabulary.definition: Take only when symptoms appear
vocabulary.context: Paracetamol 1g, oral, as needed for pain.

vocabulary.definition: Take before going to sleep
vocabulary.context: Insulin glargine 20 units at bedtime.

vocabulary.definition: Medication taken through the mouth
vocabulary.context: Most tablets are administered orally.

vocabulary.definition: Medication given directly into a vein
vocabulary.context: The antibiotic was administered intravenously.

vocabulary.definition: Medication breathed in through the mouth or nose
vocabulary.context: Salbutamol is an inhaled bronchodilator.

vocabulary.definition: Medication injected under the skin
vocabulary.context: Insulin is injected subcutaneously.

vocabulary.definition: Medication applied directly to the skin
vocabulary.context: The cream is applied topically twice daily.

vocabulary.definition: Document from a GP referring a patient to a specialist
vocabulary.context: The GP wrote a referral letter to the neurologist.
